page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-96-lssd is a high-capacity virtual machine instance belonging to the c4d server family. It is built on the x86_64 CPU architecture and features 96 dedicated vCPUs. The instance is equipped with 756.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per core.

For local storage, this server includes 3221 GB of NVMe SSD capacity distributed across 8 local SSDs. This bundled high-speed storage is integrated directly into the instance, offering low-latency data access. The configuration does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and it does not feature any GPU hardware accelerators.

From a qualitative cost efficiency perspective, the c4d-highmem-96-lssd offers a dense allocation of both memory and local NVMe storage relative to its 96 dedicated vCPUs. This makes it a resource-dense option for workloads requiring significant memory and fast local scratch space without the overhead of external storage. However, the lack of GPU acceleration and the absence of complimentary public IPv4 addresses represent notable tradeoffs for workloads requiring graphics processing or direct public internet routing.

The hardware profile of this instance makes it suitable for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. Appropriate use cases include large-scale databases, in-memory data processing, high-performance computing tasks, and complex ETL pipelines that benefit from high-speed local NVMe SSDs and a substantial memory footprint.
